subproblems.title: A.e. strong measurability of the approximate-tangent projection of an integer multiplicity triple (reused comparator-accepted declaration)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This statement is verbatim the frozen type of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.tangent_projection_measurable-a1, candidate 36b2d372). It is reused here at that identical type. The argument below is the selected parent's supplied proof, steps 1–7, ending at a.e. strong measurability.

Sources.
- Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–752): ξ is Hⁿ-measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, ξ(x) = τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space T_xM. These are the IMRep fields aestronglyMeasurable_orient and orients.
- Simon Ch. 6, 1.5–1.7 (lines 93–108): the induced inner products for which the basic (co)vectors are orthonormal. Step 3 below is the identity behind this.
- Simon Ch. 3, 1.4–1.5 (chapter-03.txt lines 75–90): the approximate tangent space, unique if it exists (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique).

Notation.
- M = R.carrier, ξ = R.orient, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M.
- e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ⟨e_i, u⟩ = u(i).
- T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x and p_x := T_x.starProjection. For a subspace Q, p_Q denotes the orthogonal projection onto Q.
- For b ∈ Fin n, succAbove_b : Fin (n−1) → Fin n is the order embedding that skips b. It is a bijection of Fin (n−1) onto Fin n ∖ {b}.

1. Case n = 0. Fix x.
- Suppose some Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M x Q. Then the `if` branch of approxTangentPlane is taken, and the chosen subspace Q₀ also satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M x Q₀ (specification of the choice). Its first conjunct gives finrank Q₀ = 0, so Q₀ = ⊥.
- Otherwise T_x = ⊥ by definition.
Hence p_x = p_⊥ = 0 for every x. A constant map is strongly measurable, so x ↦ p_x is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν. From now on n = m + 1 with m ∈ ℕ.

2. Covectors.
- For j : Fin m → Fin P, let e^j be the m-covector e^j(u_1, …, u_m) := det(u_c(j(r)))_{r,c ∈ Fin m}; for m = 0 it is the constant 1.
  - It is multilinear and alternating in (u_c): it is a determinant whose c-th column depends linearly on u_c.
  - It is continuous: it is a polynomial in finitely many coordinates.
  - In SimonGMT it is wedgeCovectors m (fun r ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (j r)); see wedgeCovectors_apply_det in Chapter06/FormsDuality.lean.
- For v ∈ ℝ^P, let α_{v,j} be the n-covector
  α_{v,j}(u_0, …, u_m) := Σ_{b=0}^{m} (−1)^b ⟨v, u_b⟩ e^j(u ∘ succAbove_b),
  where u ∘ succAbove_b = (u_0, …, û_b, …, u_m) omits u_b.
  - Equivalently α_{v,j} = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight e^j): Mathlib's alternatizeUncurryFin_apply gives exactly this sum, and alternatizeUncurryFin produces a continuous alternating map.
  - Hence α_{v,j} ∈ Covector (ℝ^P) n, and ζ(α_{v,j}) is defined for every ζ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = (Covector (ℝ^P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ).

3. Gram identity (Cauchy–Binet). For a, b : Fin m → ℝ^P,
 Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin P} e^j(a)·e^j(b) = m!·det(⟨a_r, b_c⟩)_{r,c}.
Proof.
(i) Apply the Leibniz formula to the transpose (det A = det Aᵀ = Σ_σ sgn σ Π_r A_{r,σ(r)}) with A_{r,c} = a_c(j(r)). This gives e^j(a) = Σ_{σ∈S_m} sgn σ Π_r a_{σ(r)}(j(r)). Likewise e^j(b) = Σ_{π∈S_m} sgn π Π_r b_{π(r)}(j(r)).
(ii) Multiplying and exchanging finite sums gives
 Σ_j e^j(a)e^j(b) = Σ_{σ,π} sgn σ sgn π Σ_j Π_r a_{σ(r)}(j(r)) b_{π(r)}(j(r)).
(iii) Take a sum over all functions j : Fin m → Fin P of a product whose r-th factor depends only on j(r). It equals the product over r of the sums over the value j(r). So the expression is
 Σ_{σ,π} sgn σ sgn π Π_r Σ_{i=1}^{P} a_{σ(r)}(i) b_{π(r)}(i).
(iv) In the standard orthonormal basis Σ_i u(i)w(i) = ⟨u, w⟩. So the expression is
 Σ_{σ,π} sgn σ sgn π Π_r ⟨a_{σ(r)}, b_{π(r)}⟩.
(v) Reindex the product by c = σ(r), i.e. r = σ⁻¹(c). It becomes Π_c ⟨a_c, b_{ρ(c)}⟩ with ρ := π∘σ⁻¹. Since sgn is multiplicative with values ±1, sgn ρ = sgn π·sgn σ⁻¹ = sgn σ·sgn π.
(vi) For fixed σ, π ↦ π∘σ⁻¹ is a bijection of S_m. Put G_{r,c} := ⟨a_r, b_c⟩. Then the sum equals
 Σ_σ Σ_ρ sgn ρ Π_c ⟨a_c, b_{ρ(c)}⟩ = m!·Σ_ρ sgn ρ Π_c G_{c,ρ(c)}.
By the Leibniz formula the last sum is det(Gᵀ) = det G. Hence the sum is m!·det(⟨a_r, b_c⟩). For m = 0 both sides equal 1; for P = 0 < m both sides are 0, as the argument shows uniformly.

4. Projection formula. Let Q be a subspace and ζ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) with IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q. That is, there are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q and ε ∈ {1, −1} such that ζ(α) = ε·α(τ) for every n-covector α. Then for all v, w ∈ ℝ^P,
 Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin P} ζ(α_{v,j})·ζ(α_{w,j}) = m!·⟨p_Q v, w⟩.
Proof.
(i) Deleting the b-th entry of τ gives τ∘succAbove_b. So by step 2,
 ζ(α_{v,j}) = ε Σ_b (−1)^b ⟨v, τ_b⟩ e^j(τ∘succAbove_b).
(ii) Multiply the expressions for v and w, sum over j and use ε² = 1. Then apply step 3 with a = τ∘succAbove_b and b = τ∘succAbove_{b'}:
 Σ_j ζ(α_{v,j})ζ(α_{w,j}) = Σ_{b,b'∈Fin n} (−1)^{b+b'} ⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_{b'}⟩·m!·det(⟨τ_{succAbove_b(r)}, τ_{succAbove_{b'}(c)}⟩)_{r,c}.
(iii) If b = b', the (r,c) entry is ⟨τ_{succAbove_b(r)}, τ_{succAbove_b(c)}⟩ = δ_{rc}, since τ is orthonormal and succAbove_b is injective. So the matrix is the identity, its determinant is 1, and (−1)^{2b} = 1.
(iv) If b ≠ b', then b' = succAbove_b(r₀) for some r₀, because succAbove_b maps Fin m onto Fin n ∖ {b}. Row r₀ of the matrix is (⟨τ_{b'}, τ_{succAbove_{b'}(c)}⟩)_c = 0, because succAbove_{b'}(c) ≠ b' and τ is orthonormal. A matrix with a zero row has determinant 0.
(v) Hence the sum is m!·Σ_b ⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_b⟩ = m!·⟨Σ_b ⟨τ_b, v⟩τ_b, w⟩.
Now p_Q v = Σ_b ⟨τ_b, v⟩τ_b. Indeed, w₀ := Σ_b ⟨τ_b, v⟩τ_b lies in Q, and for every c,
 ⟨τ_c, v − w₀⟩ = ⟨τ_c, v⟩ − Σ_b ⟨τ_b, v⟩⟨τ_c, τ_b⟩ = 0.
So v − w₀ is orthogonal to span(range τ) = Q, and the orthogonal projection of v is the unique w₀ ∈ Q with v − w₀ ⊥ Q. Therefore the sum is m!·⟨p_Q v, w⟩.

5. A continuous Π. Define Π : Λ_n(ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) by
 Π(ζ) := Σ_{a,b=1}^{P} g_{ab}(ζ)·L_{ab},
where
- g_{ab}(ζ) := (1/m!) Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin P} ζ(α_{e_a,j})·ζ(α_{e_b,j}), and
- L_{ab}(v) := ⟨e_a, v⟩e_b, i.e. L_{ab} = (innerSL ℝ e_a).smulRight e_b ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P).
Continuity:
- For each fixed α, the map ζ ↦ ζ(α) is continuous and linear on Λ_n(ℝ^P), since |ζ(α)| ≤ ‖ζ‖‖α‖.
- So each g_{ab} is a finite sum of products of continuous real functions, hence continuous.
- Π is a finite sum of continuous scalar functions times fixed operators, hence continuous for the operator norm.
Identification: suppose IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q. Step 4 with v = e_a, w = e_b gives g_{ab}(ζ) = ⟨p_Q e_a, e_b⟩. For every v, use v = Σ_a ⟨e_a, v⟩e_a, linearity of p_Q, and u = Σ_b ⟨u, e_b⟩e_b:
 Π(ζ)v = Σ_b Σ_a ⟨e_a, v⟩⟨p_Q e_a, e_b⟩e_b = Σ_b ⟨p_Q(Σ_a ⟨e_a,v⟩e_a), e_b⟩e_b = Σ_b ⟨p_Q v, e_b⟩e_b = p_Q v.
That is, Π(ζ) = p_Q.

6. A.e. identification.
- By the field `orients`, for ν-a.e. x there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x.
- At such x, the condition of the `if` in approxTangentPlane holds, and the chosen subspace Q' satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' (choice specification).
- HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (SimonGMT Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean; Simon Ch. 3 Remark 1.5(1)) gives Q' = Q_x.
- So T_x = Q_x and, by step 5, p_x = p_{Q_x} = Π(ξ x).

7. Conclusion.
- ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient). Choose a strongly measurable η with ξ = η ν-a.e., and simple functions η_k → η pointwise.
- Each Π∘η_k is simple, and Π∘η_k → Π∘η pointwise by continuity of Π (step 5). So Π∘η is strongly measurable.
- Π∘ξ = Π∘η ν-a.e., i.e. Π∘ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν (Mathlib: Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).
- By step 6, x ↦ p_x equals Π∘ξ ν-a.e., hence equals the strongly measurable Π∘η ν-a.e. Therefore x ↦ p_x is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν (Mathlib: AEStronglyMeasurable.congr).
Together with step 1 this proves the claim for every n, every P and every U. ∎
proof_key_steps: n = 0: approxTangentPlane is ⊥ everywhere (finrank 0), so p_x ≡ 0, which is AE-strongly measurable.
Gram (Cauchy–Binet) identity Σ_{j:Fin m→Fin P} e^j(a)e^j(b) = m!·det(⟨a_r,b_c⟩) by Leibniz expansion, product of sums, Parseval and permutation reindexing.
If ζ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ orients Q, then Σ_j ζ(α_{v,j})ζ(α_{w,j}) = m!⟨p_Q v, w⟩: diagonal minors are 1 and off-diagonal minors have a zero row.
Π(ζ) := Σ_{a,b} g_ab(ζ)·(innerSL e_a).smulRight e_b is continuous, and Π(ζ) = p_Q whenever ζ orients Q.
ν-a.e., approxTangentPlane n M x = Q_x by the choice specification and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, so p_x = Π(ξ x).
Π∘ξ is AE-strongly measurable (continuous ∘ AESM), and a.e. strong measurability transfers along the ν-a.e. equality.

subproblems.title: A.e. strongly measurable maps into L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) are a.e. measurable for its Borel σ-algebra
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ be any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). Let f : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) be a map into the space of continuous linear endomorphisms of ℝ^P, equipped with the operator-norm topology and its Borel σ-algebra (Mathlib's ContinuousLinearMap.instMeasurableSpace, which is borel). If f is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ (AEStronglyMeasurable f μ), then f is almost-everywhere measurable with respect to μ (AEMeasurable f μ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)), AEStronglyMeasurable f μ → AEMeasurable f μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the last sentence of step 7 of the selected parent's supplied proof: 'It is therefore AEMeasurable for the Borel σ-algebra of the finite-dimensional normed space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P).' Here it is stated for an arbitrary measure μ on ℝ^P and an arbitrary map f.

1. The target space. Write L := L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) = (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P).
- With the operator norm, L is a normed real vector space, hence a metric space; in particular its topology is pseudo-metrizable.
- Its measurable structure is the Borel σ-algebra of this topology. In the pinned Mathlib (MeasureTheory/Constructions/BorelSpace/ContinuousLinearMap.lean, lines 47–51), ContinuousLinearMap.instMeasurableSpace is defined as borel (E →L[𝕜] F), and ContinuousLinearMap.instBorelSpace records BorelSpace.
- For Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P the inferred instance equals borel _ by rfl.

2. A strongly measurable representative. By definition of AEStronglyMeasurable f μ, there is a strongly measurable g : ℝ^P → L with f(x) = g(x) for μ-a.e. x. Strong measurability of g means there are simple functions g_k : ℝ^P → L (k ∈ ℕ), each taking finitely many values on measurable fibres, with g_k(x) → g(x) in L for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

3. g is measurable. Let O ⊆ L be open.
- If O = L, then g⁻¹(O) = ℝ^P is measurable.
- Otherwise Oᶜ is a non-empty closed set. Then φ(y) := dist(y, Oᶜ) is a continuous (1-Lipschitz) real function on L, and O = {y : φ(y) > 0}.
  - Each φ∘g_k is a simple real function (finitely many values on the measurable fibres of g_k), hence measurable.
  - By continuity of φ, φ(g_k(x)) → φ(g(x)) for every x.
  - A pointwise limit of measurable real functions is measurable (it equals their lim sup). So φ∘g is measurable, and g⁻¹(O) = (φ∘g)⁻¹((0, ∞)) is measurable.
Since the open sets generate the Borel σ-algebra of L (step 1), g is measurable. In Mathlib this is StronglyMeasurable.measurable, which needs PseudoMetrizableSpace L and BorelSpace L.

4. Conclusion. f = g μ-a.e. and g is measurable, which is the definition of AEMeasurable f μ. In the pinned Mathlib this is AEStronglyMeasurable.aemeasurable (MeasureTheory/Function/StronglyMeasurable/AEStronglyMeasurable.lean, line 189). Its instance hypotheses PseudoMetrizableSpace L and BorelSpace L hold by step 1, so the formal proof is: intro P μ f hf; exact hf.aemeasurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: L(ℝ^P,ℝ^P) with the operator norm is a metric (pseudo-metrizable) space, and its MeasurableSpace instance is borel with BorelSpace.
AEStronglyMeasurable gives a strongly measurable g with f = g μ-a.e.
g is a pointwise limit of simple functions; testing open sets with dist(·, Oᶜ) shows g is Borel measurable.
f = g a.e. with g measurable, so AEMeasurable f μ (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.aemeasurable).
